utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Unfortunately, Judge Flugge is not able to sit this morning. We expect he will be with us again tomorrow. Judge Baird and I will sit today pursuant to Rule 15 bis. The next witness is ready, Ms. Kravetz?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The next witness is K54.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We need to go, I think, into closed session for him to come in.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I want to begin by asking the usher to hand you a piece of paper that has some personal information that relates to you. I would ask you to read that to yourself and let me know if the information on the sheet of paper is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the pseudonym sheet and the 65 ter of that is 02668, and I seek to tender that under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received in due course, Ms. Kravetz. You can move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Witness, did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecution in April 2002?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Before coming to court today, have you had the opportunity to review your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And having reviewed your statement, are you satisfied that the information contained in this statement is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, this -- the witness statement is 02676, and I seek to tender that under seal. We have also prepared a redacted public version of the statement which is 02883, and I also seek to tender that as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Those two exhibits will be received along with the pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The pseudonym sheet, Your Honours, under 65 ter 02668 would be assigned P00780 under seal. The witness statement under 65 ter 02676 will be assigned P00781 under seal. And the redacted version under 65 ter 02883 would be assigned P00782, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Witness, after having provided that statement to the Office of the Prosecution, did you tour certain localities in Kosovo with an investigator from the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did you discover the names of localities that you were not familiar with when you gave your witness statement in April 2002?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you then provide or prepare an addendum where you included the names of these localities and also provided additional information that was not included in your initial statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Have you recently had the opportunity to review the addendum to your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And are you satisfied that the information contained in this addendum is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender this addendum. The 65 ter number is 02679, and I seek to tender that version under seal. We have also prepared a public redacted version of that exhibit and that is 02884, which I also seek to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 02679 would be assigned P00783 under seal, and the redacted version under 65 ter 02884 will be assigned P00784.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now proceed to read the in-court summary of this witness's evidence. The witness was a driver in a VJ logistic corps. He describes the combat groups present in Prizren, Suva Reka, Orahovac, and Dragas areas in 1998 and 1999. He also describes combat operations in which his unit participated in the summer of 1998 and prior to and during the 1999 conflict. In February 1999, the witness was involved in an operation in Ljubizda. Later that month he took part in a large-scale operation in a village south of Prizren in which around 30 people were killed. On 25 March 1999 the witness's battalion was deployed to a village south of Mamusa in Prizren municipality along with a PJP unit. The soldiers were ordered to make sure that no one was left in the village. The witness saw soldiers force villagers, including women and children, out of a home, line them up, and shoot them in a courtyard. He estimates that around 50 to 60 civilians were killed in this operation. The witness also describes how the bodies of some of the victims were later transported to an unidentified location and buried there. The witness describes the coordination between VJ and PJP units during these joint operations. That is the end of the in-court summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I want to ask you some questions about the statement that you provided to the Office of the Prosecution. I understand from your statement that you were deployed to Prizren municipality in June of 1998 and were -- joined a VJ logistic corps as a driver; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what sort of tasks did you carry out as a driver for your unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I delivered water and food to the troops deployed on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And were you in charge of delivering food and water to all combat groups that were deployed in the area around Prizren, where your unit was deployed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nearly all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how many combat groups were deployed in that area at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you recall who was the person in charge of the combat groups that were deployed in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What was the name of the person who was in charge of those five combat groups, if you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Colonel Bozidar Delic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. Now in your statement you indicate that your -- the unit that you were attached to was deployed to a village -- the village of Damjane which, at the time, was still occupied by civilians. And you explained that Colonel Delic arrived to the village and ordered that the civilians be forced out. Did you personally see Colonel Delic at the village of Damjane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you recall what happened when he arrived there, to the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And can you tell us what happened when he arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He ordered us to force the civilians of the village out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And were those orders carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What did the soldiers do to force the civilians out of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went from one house to another and took the villagers by surprise. They threatened them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how much time were the villagers given to leave the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not more than three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were the villagers allowed to take their personal belongings with them when they left -- were ordered to leave the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just a few belongings were allowed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what happened to the personal belongings that remained in the houses of the village, the contents of the houses of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They remained behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did the army go into the houses of the village? Did the soldiers, during this operation when they were removing the villagers, did they go into the houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what happened when the soldiers were going into the houses in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would quite simply enter a house looking for gold, money, any other valuables.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And if such valuables were found by the soldiers during their house searches, what would happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would take them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we move on in your statement, you describe an operation, a mopping-up operation that took place on the road between Djakovica and Klina, and you indicate in your statement that this operation happened - this is on page 3 of your statement on the top - that this operation happened sometime between the 1st and 3rd of August. First of all, are the dates indicated in your statement correct with respect to when this operation occurred, based on the recollection you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They're not exactly accurate. The margin of error is about two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So did the operation start two or three days before the 1st of August or two or three days after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About five days before the 1st of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So if I understand correctly, it would have started sometime the last week of July 1998?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And for how many days did this operation take place? For how many days did it last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The operation lasted three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. In page 3, this is paragraph 4, you indicate that during the course of this operation your unit stopped outside a village about 15 kilometres from Djakovica. And in your addendum to your statement you have identified this village as being the village of Meca and you indicate that you were -- that Colonel Delic was close to where you were and that you heard him give the order to open fire. Can you explain what happened after Colonel Delic gave the order to open fire on the village of Meca.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The army launched an action to mop-up the area allegedly of terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And for how long did this action last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is where the action started, and it lasted for three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You say that: "The army launched an action to mop-up the area allegedly of terrorists." Can you explain what happened when this specific village was attacked, when fire was opened on this village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that women and two children exited from a house and started running in some direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did your unit enter the village after having opened fire on the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some elements of my unit did enter the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what happened when those elements of your unit entered this village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had an order to go there to clear up the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what did you understand that to mean, to clear up the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a usual term in the army, meaning to clear up, to uncover terrorists, kill them; and I think along the way to kill all the civilians that were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You mentioned having seen women and two children exit a house after fire was opened. Do you know what happened to these people, these villagers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what happened later. I know that they went out of the house, there was screaming, and they ran behind the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you said that -- I asked you what the term to clear up the area meant, and you said that it was a usual term used to uncover terrorists and along the way kill all civilians that were there. Did you have instructions to kill all civilians that were in the village? Were those the instructions that your unit was given?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I see my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wrote down what the witness said to the previous question. The witness says the clearing up involves killing and finding civilians and that he thinks, that he thinks, that that -- that civilians would be taken care of along the way and that was his opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's what the transcript discloses, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but now Mrs. Kravetz is saying, When you received -- or When did you receive orders to kill civilians?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: She started saying that, I agree, but she turned it then into a question, recognising your point, and asked specifically: "Did you have instructions to kill all civilians ..." And that's the question to which an answer is now awaited. Carry on, Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall my question, or should I repeat it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can give you an answer. It went without saying that everything should be cleared up once such an order is issued, and that means to kill everyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When elements of your unit went into that village, did they discover any elements of the KLA in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about that. There were some rumours or stories that those were terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Other than those -- the women and children that you've spoken about, did you see any other civilians in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you continue on from that village after this operation was completed in the village of Meca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we proceeded.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And was -- were any MUP units involved in this action, this operation that you've been speaking about that happened toward the end of July and lasted for about three days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were members of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And during this operation that you conducted with elements of the MUP, what were the tasks that were carried out by the MUP units during the conduct of this clean-up operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They carried out their operation ahead of the army, and we came as assistance and support. They had been there before we arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what sort of assistance or support did your VJ unit provide to the MUP units that were engaged in this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did more or less the similar things to what they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did your -- the units of your battalion, did they have any sort of heavy weaponry or tanks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were tanks and Pragas.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did the MUP units that were involved in this action have any sort of heavy weaponry or tanks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They used our army tanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. You said that the MUP units would precede the VJ units in this action. Would the tanks be attached to the VJ unit when the action was being carried out, or would the MUP unit that would precede your unit be using the tanks during this sort of clean-up operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they used our tanks while we were there, so as I said, we provided support and this is the way in which they used the tanks, so through us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So if I understand correctly, it would be the VJ unit who would be providing fire support to the MUP during the operation; that's what you're saying? Not that the MUP unit would be using the tanks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now I want to move a bit forward in time to an action that you describe in your statement, and this is an action that took place in the village of Jeskovo. You say in your statement that around the second week of March 1999 you were involved in an action about 7 to 8 kilometres south of the Prizren-Zur road and you've identified that in your -- in the addendum to your statement - and this is at the bottom of page 4 - as the village of Jeskovo. And you say on page 5 of your statement that you recall Colonel Delic giving the order to fire -- open fire on the village of Jeskovo. First of all, do you recall being involved in an action around the second week of March in the area of the village of Jeskovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you recall hearing Colonel Delic issue instructions to open fire on the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Before your units opened fire on the village of Jeskovo, was there any outgoing fire towards the positions where your units were located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You explain in your statement that fire -- that you fired on the village for approximately half an hour and then you rested. After the firing took place, did you hear Colonel Delic give any further orders or issue any further tasks to your unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before that fire that you mentioned, before that fire, Colonel Delic ordered -- he said, At my sign once the first shell hits the village, open the fire to that village. So we fired for approximately half an hour, then the firing stopped. We stayed for a while. Then once we heard a shot again, we resumed firing. I can't really tell you how long this time around it lasted. Then when it stopped, we waited for a longer period of time to make sure that there were no further signs of life from that village, and then he ordered that we should go down and clear up the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what happened when the soldiers of your unit entered the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simply, if there was anyone left alive they would kill that person and there were many dead persons around.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you personally see any of the persons who had been killed during the shelling or by fellow soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once we came down to the village, I personally saw dead civilians as we came down to the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And at any point was there any sort of fire coming out from the village after the village had been attacked towards the positions of your unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember any.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Was there -- were there any MUP units involved in this action on the village of Jeskovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what sort of tasks did the MUP units carry out during this action on the village of Jeskovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They started the action first, so that was the task, to start the action first.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you say "they started the action," what exactly did they do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when we came down to the village, as we arrived there I personally found MUP personnel there, but I didn't see precisely what it was they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So did they enter the village before your VJ unit entered the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And we were speaking about the order given by Colonel Delic to fire on the village, was your VJ unit the only one involved in firing on the village or were MUP units also firing on the village before you entered it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Ms. Kravetz kindly speak closer to her microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were approximately 1.300 men, as far as I heard, on that day. Approximately 1.000 were soldiers and the remaining number were police officers. I know that the village was encircled.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. And my question was whether only the VJ units fired on the village or if the MUP units were also involved in firing on the village before you entered it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both the army and the police were firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to move to another action that you describe in your statement. This is an action that took place on the 25th of March south of a village called Mamusa. And in your addendum to your statement you have indicated that the name of the village is the village of Trnje, although in this statement it had been initially indicated as the village of Medvec, but you've corrected that in the addendum. Do you recall taking part in an action on the village of -- or against the village of Trnje on 25th March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And were MUP units also involved in this action on the village of Trnje ? Was it also a joint MUP/VJ action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they also participated in it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did soldiers of your unit enter the village of Trnje during the course of this action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what did they do when they entered the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They killed the population of the village and set the houses on fire, and they set belongings of the population on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you said that they killed the population of the village. Did you personally witness any of these killings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the incident that you witnessed when villagers were killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw the population of the village at the beginning of this operation. When the soldiers came into the village the population started to flee through the meadows. Some of them were unaware of what was happening. I saw them running away, the elderly, women, everybody. They started to flee over meadows and cultivated land, and they simply fell down when they were shot.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You said that you saw elderly and women starting to flee and that they fell down when they were shot. Where -- did you find any men in the village, men of military age in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Possibly there were but just a few.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did soldiers enter the houses of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what would happen when the soldiers would enter the houses in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the operation, if they found anybody in the house they would take them out or possibly they would even do it in the house, but usually they would take them out of the house and kill them in the courtyard or wherever they found persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: In your statement, you indicate that approximately 50 to 60 persons were killed during this operation. Can you tell us anything about the age and the sex of these victims from what you remember generally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When it comes to their age, there were elderly people, elderly women and men, and one part of them were young girls and the remaining number were children.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you know why the population of this village was killed in the manner that you have described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, earlier you said that the houses in the village were also set on fire. Were you personally involved in any of the or in setting on fire any houses in that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I personally set one house on fire, one bus. I was ordered to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know why houses were set on fire in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that. Probably to prevent the population from coming back.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were any MUP units involved in this action against the village of Trnje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what was the role of the MUP units during the course of this action? What did they do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came from the opposite direction, and they initiated the operation, whereas we waited for the alleged terrorists to come out if they would start to flee.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You said you "waited for the alleged terrorists to come out if they would start to flee." Did you see any members of the KLA fleeing the village before you entered it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did MUP units also -- the MUP units that were involved in this action, did they also enter the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what did they do when they entered the village? Were they also involved in house-to-house searches like the ones that you've described your unit was involved in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what would happen when they would enter the houses of the inhabitants of the village, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We knew that they would usually come in a house searching for gold, money, or anything similar, so any valuables. And if they found anybody alive, they would kill him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if we could very briefly go into private session just to clarify a previous answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, on page 6 of your statement you say that after this action of Trnje was concluded you returned to the barracks in Prizren and discovered that the barracks had been bombed, and that you went to a settlement below the barracks and were ordered to expel the civilians in that area and take up residence in the houses. For how long did you remain in this settlement close to the town of Prizren?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Throughout the shelling. For as long as the shelling in Kosovo lasted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, the civilians that were in this settlement, in which direction were they sent? Where were they told to go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were not really interested in where they went. Possibly they went to stay with their family, with their relatives, and later on they went in the direction of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: At the beginning of your testimony you told us that you worked as a driver for your unit. While you were carrying out your tasks as a driver, did you come across any civilians in the area of Prizren on the roads in the area of Prizren?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you recall when and how many civilians you saw on the roads in the area of Prizren?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, every day I saw civilians walking or being driven by trucks in the direction of Albania, so it was a mass exodus of population of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You say that every day you saw civilians walking or being driven by truck in the direction of Albania. Can you tell us from where these civilians were coming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were coming from the direction of Suva Reka and Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And these civilians that were coming from the direction of Djakovica and Suva Reka, do you recall on which road they were travelling, which road they were heading in the direction of for Albania?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had to use the main roads. They were not allowed to use any other roads, given that from the direction of Djakovica towards Prizren and from the direction of Suva Reka towards Prizren there are main roads -- they were allowed only to use the main roads and allegedly the army would not touch them as long as they stayed on the main road.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You say that every day you saw civilians walking or being driven on these main roads. Do you recall when you started seeing the civilians heading down the main roads from Suva Reka and Djakovica in the direction of Albania?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started seeing them approximately day five or day six of the shelling, and from there on it continued.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say "day five or day six of the shelling," which shelling are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm talking about bombing rather than shelling, bombing by NATO.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say you saw civilians heading down these roads in the direction of Albania, can you tell us approximately how many civilians you would see on -- heading down -- are you talking about small groups of 10, 20 persons? Or are you talking of larger groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't believe anybody could count these people. There were very many persons. This was a mass phenomenon. People walked in groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were large groups, numerous groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did you see any police presence on the road while these persons were heading in the direction of Albania down the main roads as you were driving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you recall what the policemen that you saw on the roads were doing as these civilians were travelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember that precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were these policemen that you saw stationed anywhere along the roads or did you just see them travelling down the roads in the same manner that you travelled down the roads during this period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They moved more around the towns, but they were all over the place.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in your statement you say that after the operation in Trnje you were ordered to take a civilian truck and pick up bodies and you were ordered to collect the bodies of women and children. And you say: "However, the bodies of the children and most of the women were no longer there." Just to clarify when you're talking about the bodies of the women and most of the children being no longer there, are you speaking about the same action we spoke about earlier in the village of Trnje or are you speaking about some other village where you went to collect the bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was speaking about the Trnje action.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, do you know -- when you say that most of the bodies of the women and children were no longer there, do you know who took them, what happened to the bodies of the women and the children that had been killed in this action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before arrival in the village the following day, we found PJP there and they had carried the bodies away before we arrived. That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And who told you that, that the PJP had carried the bodies away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard it from my captain, who I drove on that day and who was with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you say that you collected the bodies of five women and you indicate in your statement that you drove the truck south towards the border and at some point you got off the border and proceeded to bury the bodies there. While you were travelling to this locality towards -- south towards the border, were you escorted by anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had escort.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know why the bodies were -- of these five women were buried there in -- off the road that you were travelling in this unidentified location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know why, but I know that we buried them so that no one could see them and so that no one could know where they were buried. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know whether the bodies of these five women have since been found, the location of where they were buried has been identified?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know they were. We did make an effort to -- did this in a safe and secure way, but somebody apparently had seen us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. And when were they found, the location where these bodies were found -- buried?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About ten days after the NATO forces entered Kosovo, I heard that. That's what I heard allegedly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will ask very briefly to go into private session again to ask some additional questions on a different topic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, in the addendum to your statement you indicate - and this is on page 2 - that it was common knowledge from soldiers talking to other soldiers that there were orders for police and VJ to take all the ID documents from Albanians at the borders and burn them to prevent them from claiming they were from Kosovo. Can you tell us how you know that, where you heard that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was talk about that, that documents were being seized from Albanians at the border crossing, the Albanians who were leaving Kosovo. They were just piled up and set on fire, and since the fire was burning they would just add new documents to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You said "there was talk about that." Do you recall whom you spoke to about this, who told you that this is what was happening at the border?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was one man from the area where I hailed from and he was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say "he was there," where was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the spot, on the border crossing where the documents were being burned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So if I understand correctly, this man is the person who told you that this was happening at the border, or am I misunderstanding your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he was at the border.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And he's the person who spoke to you about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. And was this someone from your same unit, this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when did you speak to him? Was this while the conflict was still going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes -- while the bombing was in progress, is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I just have very few questions left. Moving on to June 1999 you say that -- in your statement on page 7 that you left Kosovo on 6 June and you got on a bus from Pristina to Mitrovica, where you changed buses. And you say: "It was like hell. I saw many burning houses and PJP officers walking around shooting." Can you indicate which town you're referring to when -- where you saw many burning houses and PJP officers walking around shooting. Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the bus station in Kosovska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And can you tell us why it is that you left Kosovo on 6 June 1999.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went on a deserved weekend leave, but there was another reason for my insisting on leaving.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What was that reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since the majority of officers had already confiscated good-quality cars and trucks, I didn't want simply to drive any of those cars or trucks full of things that were taken out of people's houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You say that the majority of officers had confiscated good-quality cars and trucks and they were full of things taken out of people's houses. Which houses are you speaking about that the goods were taken out of, whose houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said Albanian houses, the Albanian local population.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you say that the majority of officers had taken these cars, were these officers from your same brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both from our units and other units as well, because a brigade is rather a large unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And was this -- this confiscation of good-quality cars and the taking of things from the houses, is this something that had happened in June or had it happened earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It did happen earlier too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But when you say you left in June and you gave this reason, was this something that was happening at the time that made you decide to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, while I was there, there was confiscation of property and cars, and when I left my home and went to the barracks in Leskovac I heard that some officers had loaded trucks with belongings and things taken from the Albanian houses and that they were transporting them to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Just to be clear on the time-period, when you say you left your home and went to the barracks in Leskovac, are you speaking about June 1999 or about another period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I left six days before the army's withdrawal from Kosovo, that is to say the army withdrew, and when they arrived in Leskovac they summoned me to come to Leskovac to return the issued equipment. And I stayed there for about ten days; it's a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So you are speaking about the period of June 1999 if I'm correct when you say some officers had loaded trucks with belongings and things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djurdjic, would you like to have the break now or would you like to cross-examine for ten minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it would be more beneficial to have a break now and then we continue uninterrupted; but if you think that another approach is better, I will go along with your decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it would be more use to everybody if you could think about things during the break and the witness will be able to refresh himself. We need to go into closed session because of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic now has some questions for you. Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, do you allow me to address you Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's all the same to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My name is Veljko Djurdjic. I am a member of the accused Vlastimir Djordjevic's Defence team, and Ms. Marie O'Leary is another team member here present. Before I begin with my questions, I would kindly ask you to wait for a few moments after I finished my questions so that interpreters can finish their job and translate accurately what we are speaking because we speak the same language. Mr. Witness, I would like to ask you, Do you remember better today the events that you described or was that the case at the time when you gave either a written statement or -- statement or when you gave evidence in two trials before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it is only natural that my memory was best when I gave my first statement, and my memory doesn't serve me that well after ten years.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I started with this question and I'll tackle certain things that you mentioned today but which I was unable to notice in your statements, and I did read all your statements given thus far. Mr. Witness, today you said at the beginning of the examination by my learned colleague Ms. Kravetz that you had learned the names of some localities at the time when you gave the second statement. Can you tell me how did you find out about these names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was on the ground when I was giving statement, and I spent a few days on the location with a person from The Hague Tribunal to show him these particular places and he wrote down the names of those places.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me who accompanied you on those trips?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A certain Jonathan, a driver, and myself. Actually, he was not a driver, he was a security guard, while Jonathan was driving the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: May I then conclude that there were two of you and a security guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the total --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness and the counsel are overlapping.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot tell you that. We can go into the closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Although these other persons are probably not, Your Honours, can we now move into a private session or a closed session, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I understood that there was a person accompanying you who is an investigator. How many other persons besides those previously mentioned accompanied you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In total there were four of us: The investigator, the security guard, me, and a friend of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see who the investigator was. Who was this fourth person, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a security guard from a security agency. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you know him from before, which language he spoke?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a black man. He spoke English. I don't know where he came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which language did you use?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise, I apologise. I forgot about an interpreter. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you then please tell us when did this interpreter join you and who that was, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the name. The interpreter introduced himself or herself, but I forgot the name. I apologise once again. I forgot about the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That is quite all right. Can you just tell me when -- where did the interpreter join you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an Albanian, and he joined us -- I believe that he came along with Jonathan. They waited for me in Pec, in the town of Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me how it happened, how it came about, that you went to Pec on the 8th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the investigator to whom I gave my first statement arranged for this. I actually requested this from him. I requested to go there and to indicate in the field these places, and he made sure this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the same investigator was present on the second occasion or was it a different investigator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You said that you requested this from the investigator that you spoke to on the first time, so I'm just asking: Was it the same investigator who accompanied you when you went to the field to show these villages, or was it a different person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a different person. It was not the same investigator. The name of the first investigator was John Zdrilic. The name of the second one was Jonathan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Another thing, when and where did you sign the document about your trip to various localities in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember the date, but it was in Budva.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was present on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Myself, the investigator, and an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which investigator was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jonathan Zdrilic -- sorry, no, John Zdrilic, not Jonathan but John Zdrilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Not only that -- at that time you said you visited these localities but you also made an addendum?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So the addendum containing information that you did not include in your original statement from April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, in this statement I can not see that it was signed. Was there an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't really remember. I believe there was one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When you saw the statement, when you went to Budva, in which form was this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't understand this question. What do you mean in what form?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I will explain. So you talked verbally and then you also signed a written statement. When was this written statement made? Was it already waiting for you when you came to Budva?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was the statement that I made on that occasion. I spoke to that person for full five hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the day I came to Budva. I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No. I'm now asking for the second time you spoke to them after you went to Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. So after I saw the localities in Kosovo, I can't remember that I signed anything afterwards. We visited these localities, and for security reasons I acted that I was a member of a foreign agency. So I feared all the time that somebody could recognise me. I can't really remember that I signed anything at that time. Possibly I did, but I can't remember. It is probably even that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me something about that security issue when you visited localities in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I requested, if possible, to show them these localities, but I was afraid that somebody could recognise me as a previous soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So how did you go about that? How were you secured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were in a foreign vehicle, so the population I assume could think that these were all foreigners.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But you moved around. Did you go to different houses, different facilities that you talked about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and Jonathan made quite a few photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Speaking about photographs, did you see these photographs today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see these photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you went there, you indicated these localities. Did you afterwards see anybody from the Tribunal? So as far as I heard there was no written document composed at the time. You went back to Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So what followed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the meantime it just so happened that I lost the phone number and I took a new one, so for several months, for two or three months or after two or three months by accident I called Zdrilic. This could be some 12 or 13 days before I came to The Hague first time, so immediately after I called him I was invited to come to The Hague for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, no, let us clarify this. How many days after your return from this trip around Kosovo were you in contact with somebody from the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several months afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where was that contact established, in which country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I need to ask you, this is an exhibit I believe P783.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we kindly have that on the screen, page 2, please, in the English version and in the Serbian version I believe it's the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, is this your signature that you can see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see the date here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 16th July, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. And do you remember when it was that you took this trip around Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please remember this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would kindly ask for the first page to be shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see the very beginning of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe if we could see the B/C/S version -- oh, it is here on the left. Sorry, I didn't realise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see the beginning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it says on Monday, 8th July, 2002, I accompanied investigator -- this is Jonathan, Jonathan Sutch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, and on the last page of the document the date was the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, you said you were in the contact several months after and here it says the 8th of July and the end of the document it says 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they probably know that better. As I said, I couldn't remember exactly when it was that I made that trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever read the version in the B/C/S before you signed this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you explain the issue here, is it the issue of the dates or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: There are several issues here. First of all, you said that several months after you visited these places in Kosovo you went to Sarajevo and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, this is what was recorded in the transcript, this is what you said. And then you explained why you came to Sarajevo so late.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I went to Sarajevo to have my visa put into my passport. This is why I went to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. But what about this statement now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't really remember how much time elapsed. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, my question was: Do you even remember where you signed this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I signed this statement to Jonathan probably -- I can't even remember where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How many days after the trip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember. That was long time ago. It was back in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. But do you remember how you read this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I can't even remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who else was present besides the two of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, probably an interpreter and that friend of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see that aside from your signature there is no other name and no other signature of this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know what that means.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you write down the names of the localities that you visited?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He wrote them down, the investigator wrote them down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that an entire name, an entire locality was recorded erroneously, wrongly? You were talking about two different geographical areas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I took him to the place where I was supposed to take him to. How he recorded it I don't know and what the interpreter told him I don't know. I really don't know what was it that he wrote down, but I showed him the places he was supposed to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come back to that later on. Today at the beginning of your testimony you said that you worked as a driver of a logistic corps. I believe this is what was recorded by the transcript. Am I true that there is no logistic corps, that this doesn't really exist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. Maybe I said it wrongly, maybe it was recorded wrongly. It was meant to be logistic battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Please do not mention any numbers or anything that could identify you. What was the name, without the number of the unit, that you were a member of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know the name if there was any name of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned the term combat group. What does that actually mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I started to go to the field, the officers were talking about establishing a combat group or setting up a combat group which was supposed to go to the field and spent three or four days, maybe a week, but we stayed there for a longer period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let us just clarify this. So you are a driver by qualification -- sorry, by your military specialty --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: -- you are a driver?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: During the course of the war, did you only act as a driver or did you have other roles as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had other roles as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you work as an infantry man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to show to you something new, at least to me. And in that sense can we please have document P778 -- that's your 2001 statement, but I think it's under the seal. Could we then use another one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Exhibit P781 is the redacted version of the first statement. Is that what you want?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, 782.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it doesn't make any difference if it is redacted or not redacted. I would have preferred it not redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Witness, I would ask you not to mention any names.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You said that you had heard that the unit commander had said that all the civilians in the village of Damjan should move. In your first statement you said that you had heard that from a conversation with a soldier who was conversing with Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: From ... ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard it personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But you didn't say "personally" in your first statement. You said, I talked to a soldier who overheard Delic issuing the order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In order to confirm what I had heard, I asked the soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But you didn't mention that on the first occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Further on you said that the soldiers and other officers were stealing things from houses. Did you steal as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you report these thefts to anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no need for me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: There was no need for you to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move to page 3 of this same document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's been almost ten years since 1999, and today we have corrected some dates, haven't we. How come that all of a sudden you now remember the dates ten years ago and a minute ago you couldn't remember the lapse of time of eight days? And I'm specifically talking about passage three and August -- how come that you remember today that it was in the last week of July and you couldn't remember that before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went home on the 3rd of August. When I gave my statement, I was trying to remember those days, I couldn't remember, and that's how I put it. Allow me to finish, please. Two days ago I called a friend of mine who was with me on the spot, and I asked him about the exact dates. This action was launched on the 24th of July, 1998. So when I went to the barracks I was supposed to be transported in a military convoy. I spent some time there. Then we set off from the barracks towards Djakovica. Then it took some time, it took a few days. I know that we spent three nights in those villages because these villages are close to one another, and I considered that to be one village. So after the three nights, we went back to the barracks. So we travelled almost the whole day and the whole night. And I had to call my friend to confirm and to give me the exact dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I really admire your memory of dates. Of course you can make a mistake, but it -- what I find interesting is that after ten years you decided to change the dates. Can you tell me who did you call?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I called a friend of mine who was with me on the ground in those days and took part in the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where did you call him from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We are going too fast, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you called him from The Hague. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm just reading it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: "When the shell fell, people could be seen running around the village. It was assumed that there were no civilians in the village, and everyone started firing guns of all descriptions." Is this what it says here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't find that portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, starting from the top it says: "I was standing near my combat unit commander ..." And then fifth line down when it says "...when the shell fell...," this is a portion I read out to you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Doesn't it say here that you were surprised to see people moving around because you hadn't expected that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We hadn't expected that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And after that, fire was opened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fire started immediately; and as soon as it started, we saw it. But as soon as this shell fell, the civilians or who else, because we were looking from a hill, we saw them started running.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And after that fire started --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would kindly ask my learned colleague to allow the witness to complete his answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, I put my hand up because you were overlapping with the witness again, Mr. Djurdjic. You become too excited and involved and you butt in. You need to let the witness finish his answer just as he needs to let you finish your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In order not to repeat the same mistake again, let us try to wait for the transcript to be finished and then we can start talking. So please take a look at the cursor; when it stops, you can start answering. I'm not sure what was included in the transcript now, this is why I'm looking at it. Am I right to say after this shell fell, once people started running around the village, that is when the fire was opened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we've come to the village of Trnje. This is supposed to be on page 6 of the B/C/S version and page 5 in the English version. Today you told us - and I wrote it down, this is on page 16 of the transcript, lines 9 to 15 - I saw personally the civilians fleeing after the soldiers entered the village and I saw them falling down as they ran across meadows and cultivated land. Did I hear this well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But in your statement of 2002 there is no mention of this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Possibly I mentioned a different word there when I talked about the cultivated land.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, you didn't. There was no mention of people fleeing across meadows, army shooting them, and these civilians falling down. I will tell you later on what you did say, but this is something that I have heard today for the first time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when somebody flees a house in a village, where is that person supposed to flee, if there are meadows, cultivated land, or woods around the village? So in your mind where are they supposed to flee?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Maybe you didn't understand my question. I put it to you that today you stated that you saw people falling down and soldiers shooting at people running across meadows or cultivated land. All I'm saying is that there is no such content in your statement made in April of 2002 and later amended in August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe I said a different version, maybe I put it differently at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now that we've mentioned this and in order to prevent coming back to this issue, at the end of this paragraph - and this is the last paragraph in B/C/S, paragraph 8, and in the English version this is paragraph 2 on page 6 - you say: "I'm not sure about the exact number of the victims, but I think there were 50 to 60. I estimate this from listening to all the soldiers talking and boasting about the number of people they killed." So the number of people is not the number of bodies you saw, but you heard this from other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is not your personal experience. Today you stated that in this village you also saw MUP units when you described what went on at the time when you entered the village. Did I understand this correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see MUP members on that occasion, but they were there in these days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, we have to clarify this. Today when my learned colleague asked you this, and she asked when you entered the village whether members of MUP were there, it entered into transcript that you said that was the case. So I'm asking this again. Were they present on the first day when you came to the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were not there on that first day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify another point. Paragraph 3 on page 6 of the English version of your statement. Now that you explained what the situation was like, here you said: "We returned to the hill and remained there in support of PJP for five days. While we were there, we would fire at the direction of the terrorists." Is this true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Then you go on saying: "On the fifth day through binoculars I could see the PJP heading in our direction, and I realised that the operation was complete." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And then you explained that you returned to Prizren. We've clarified that already. Thank you. Now I'm coming to the part -- please allow me just one second. Once again, without mentioning any names, on page 7 in the B/C/S version, did you hear your immediately superior at the level of a company issuing orders relating to civilians, to what needs to be done with the civilians during this operation that took place on the 25th of March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you personally heard that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So we are still at the same page of the transcript -- of the statement. Today you stated in relation to paragraph 3 of your statement that when you came to the scene, the bodies were not there because before coming to the village you came across PJP and they took away the bodies. There is no such content in your statement of 2002 to the fact that PJP took away any bodies. Can you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You can take a look at paragraph 3. There is nothing to that extent in your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you said that you heard this for the first time from this captain - I don't want to mention his name - when you drove him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Another question: Do you know who is on trial in this particular case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know who he was, so which part of -- which units he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that precisely, but I can imagine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was he a military person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did he work in the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that he had to do with the state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. That is part of the police affairs as well. So I have to ask you now, how come that ten years later you are mentioning police units and you did not mention them in 2002?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when I gave my statement, I focused on the military; but there were also mixed situations where the police was also there. But they asked me precisely about the military activities. I never knew that I was going to come to testify in a case against a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Hold on, but you testified in Milutinovic case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And there was another police officer that was on trial there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I'm coming to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise, but in my statement I did mention PJP in a place between Djakovica and Klina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I did not say you did not mention PJP. I'm just saying that you did not mention PJP in the context we have just discussed now. Let us proceed. When we are talking about the place where you buried these five persons, you said somebody obviously identified the place where they were buried. How did you come up with such a conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the first investigator, John Zdrilic, told me that. And the person described him exactly the situation which took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You did not go there to show them the place, so when you toured the locations in Kosovo after the war you did not show them the place where the bodies were buried?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because the time was short. We could not do everything. It was almost dark, and I simply indicated the direction, in the direction of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Or did he tell you that he knew where it was so it wasn't necessary for you to indicate it precisely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I told him it is over there in that mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you that he knew already where it was and it wasn't necessary for you to indicate it precisely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact words of the interpreter who was talking to me, but it was too dangerous to go there since it was almost dark. I spent that entire day explaining to him what happened where.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can we now turn to your second statement, or rather, the addendum from July 2002. I believe this is the Exhibit P783. At the end of this statement you're saying as a supplement of the statement I gave, "so two or three months ago --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Two or three months later.
