utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: -- no, I apologise, this is the very last page of the statement. This is the one that I'm referring to right now. You simply said you that heard about these documents from the conversations between soldiers, and you said that they were orders from the military and from the police. Have you personally heard this order from either military or the police to destroy the documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The person that you heard that from, what was that person engaged in, so what was his job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a person who comes from the same area from which I come, and he was in charge of the technical company in my battalion. But he made some mistakes, and that's why he was transferred to the infantry, and he took part in this, he saw this in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you ever at the border crossing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there are no military personnel at the border, there are simply civilian personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What about military border posts? I assume that during the war they were together, and I do know that the police is usually at the border crossings. However, the military border post is maybe 50 or 100 metres away from the border crossing.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please remove his hand from his face. The interpreters can't hear him well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If I could now move to the period of June 1999. You said, if I'm not mistaken, that on the 6th of June you went for a deserved weekend vacation; am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me how you deserved this weekend, why were you awarded this weekend off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was given a weekend off by the captain whom I drove during the bombardment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The right captain or his deputy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you why was he giving you this weekend off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, for treating him well and for obeying him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you maybe take away the stuff that he looted from the houses? Did you transport his -- that stuff to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you transport any looted stuff by -- that was looted by anybody else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, you said that there were thefts of property from the houses. How do you know who these houses belonged to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I simply knew who they belonged to. They were Albanians there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we saw the Albanian flags and their pictures -- well, one simply knows who lives there, although I must say that there were other ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Non-Albanians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were non-Albanians whom we did not expel from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: From what houses? I just ask you generally how do you know that all the houses that had been looted were Albanian houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But we expelled only Albanians from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: From where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the village which is close to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We are not there yet. We didn't understand each other at all. We are not talking about the barracks in Prizren at all. I am talking about the looting of the houses in the villages, in the country-side. How did you know that things were being stolen from the Albanian houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were there any non-Albanians in those villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the Albanian villages were only Albanians, and this was done in the Albanian villages only. And I'm telling you this where we expelled people from, I'm talking about one neighbourhood of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And I told you that I didn't ask you about that, that we'll discuss that later. I'm asking you about the villages. Who told you that there were no non-Albanians in those villages, and therefore you concluded that all the houses were Albanian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard it from our non-commissioned officers. We were in contact with them, we talked with them, we were living like a family and we discussed things amongst ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: During that operation you passed through Zociste, Velika Hoca, Mala Hoca, Retimlje, do these names mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard about Hoca and Zociste, but I can't remember about Retimlje. Since all these villages are clustered and close to one another, we just called them by one name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So according to you, that one single name was the Albanian villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but it depended on which particular area you're referring to. The one between Prizren and Djakovica, on the left-hand side, there was not a single Serbian village. Those were purely Albanian villages. And in the environs of Prizren, there are some Serbian villages, some Bosniak villages, and some Albanian villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When you say on the way from Djakovica down the Drin on the left-hand side; however, the right-hand side of the road towards Orahovac and this operation between the 25th and 30th, am I right to say that there are Serbian villages there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I would like now to move to the questions of a more general nature. Where did you give your first statement in April --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You already asked me that. It was in Budva.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This hasn't been noted, but you did tell us that today. How about your second statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them I gave in Sarajevo, and some I've no idea. There was some annexes and addenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How did it come about for you to give a statement to a Tribunal investigator in April 2002?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They called me by phone. I don't know how they got my number. They asked me if I was willing to talk to them. They had some questions for me and wanted to know if I was willing to give a statement, and of course I said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ask them how they had reached you in particular?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. But I didn't get any answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That means that some of your friends has recommended you?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me something about your educational background.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I completed secondary school of transportation, and I'm a driver by profession.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can we say the name where you lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is the same place where you said your friend was from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you live in that same place before you went to the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What were you doing for living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a taxi-driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What was your mother's name?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I would like to know about this conversation between the commander and the tank driver that you talked about. Where was the tank driver in the tank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in the tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But you said you heard a conversation between the commander and the tank driver?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that was not exactly the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's what's written.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but this was not exactly the case. Any tank had its officer. The tank was parked and the driver had nothing to do with the commander, but obviously the tank -- commander officer obviously dealt with the colonel. However, obviously everybody in the tank had their earphones within the helmets that they had and he transferred this order to person in the turret.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. So after the 8th of July, you went to show to the investigator this house that was fired on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you show him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And did you take pictures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see those pictures afterwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the next page, that's page 3, Article 6 -- paragraph 6, you said: "Then we went to a different village that was some 5 to 6 kilometres away ..." You didn't mention the name of this village. Do you know now what was the name of that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It may have been Drenovac or something similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Furthermore you said that there was a PJP unit from Djakovica there. Did you speak to any member of that unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How do you know that they belonged to that unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were there in large numbers. They were there before we came, and when we came I saw them in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But you didn't talk to any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you were fired on, if I'm not mistaken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a bit later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that one of the -- one policeman was shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him fall, but later on due to panic I did not pay much attention to what happened to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. And then on August the 3rd you went home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was even before, but this is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So if I'm not mistaken, you went home even on the 1st?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I would like to know in February of 1999 that you were in Ljubizda Has, in -- the best bakers in Serbia come from that place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was there KLA present in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were there any ambushes there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This was at a time when the verifiers were already there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you see any of them. Mr. Witness, did you have any direct contact with the verifiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not personally, but I was in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can we now move to Jeska [as interpreted]. You said that this was two weeks later after Ljubizda Has.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is not what I said. Possibly this was recorded mistakenly. I may have said two or three months later and this was somehow recorded wrongly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify this. You said that on the 28th of February you were in Ljubizda Has and Jeskovo was before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The 28th of February, that was before the war, and this was -- no, Jeskovo was also before the war. But possibly when I made my statement I put in wrong dates. Maybe they corrected it later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I don't believe so, but please take a look at your statement and you can recall what you said. Did anybody tell you why you went to Jeskovo and what was the goal of that action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the only occasion when we were told why we went somewhere, and on that occasion I insisted to participate in this action. And this is why I was engaged as an infantryman.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So which types of units participated in this action on Jeskovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean what type of unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, without me indicating any answers, you mentioned some groups, so which groups you participated in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were not groups, but soldiers were taken from the barracks, a certain number of soldiers were taken from the barracks. I was in a barracks during that time, so the alert was sounded. I know -- I'm sure that you know what it looks like when the alert is sounded, but we knew in advance where we were supposed to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So what did they tell you, where were you going?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told that we were going to a village near Zur or Dragas.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because there were terrorists there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you have any radios -- or did you personally have a radio transmitter while you were in the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have it personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which of the commanders had them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All officers and non-commissioned officers had radio transmitters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When I served in the military we used the so-called RUPs, R-U-Ps. Were you also using them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, now we have something similar to police radio transmitters. The RUPs are not used anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So during the war you also used those transmitters where you speak in such a way that anybody can hear you, anybody can hear the air transmission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, these were the transmitters used.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I now kindly have the Exhibit D003-225 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: There is no need for you to read this now, but I will kindly ask my associate to read out one part of the text, and I will tell you, this is a report by the Kosovo Verification Mission dated 11th of March, 1999. So I would kindly ask my associate to read out this portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, due to the language issues, would it be all right for my associate to read out this portion?

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: "Prizren Regional Centre comments that the KLA had infiltrated into Jeskovo, a previously deserted village, approximately one week ago. Residents in Hoca Zagradska had informed the OSCE of their concern at the KLA move."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document you mentioned can't be found in e-court with that number, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D003-0225. My associate usually makes no mistake about this, so it must be there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You put an extra zero in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's quite possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, this was just an illustration. You see that the monitors also knew that KLA was present in Jeskovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand they knew this, but why did they prevent them from coming any closer to the road --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you know they were there all the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let us repeat this. So did you know they were present there all the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you did not know that. Let me show you then a report of the OSCE dated 12th of March, 1999, about their findings on the situation in Jeskovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is document D003-0227, and I will kindly ask, again, my associate to read out a portion. This is on page 2 of this document. On the first page you can see the date of the report, and on the second page you can see the portion of the text that will now be read out.

utterances.speaker: MS. O'LEARY
utterances.text: CS 20A and 20B accompanied Colonel Petrovic and the milicija into Jeskovo whilst they carried out an investigation into yesterday's VJ operation in the village. Seven KLA bodies were found to the north of and on the outskirts of the village. All were dressed in black coveralls (KLA uniform) and had apparently died from small arms fire. In the vicinity of each body was an AK series weapon and at one location an LMG weapon with drum magazine."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you can hear this. On the second day they went out to make an inspection, if that's what you would call it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And what about the first day, where were they?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But they were at the entrance as you could hear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The operation was completed before the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So do you mean that representatives of the OSCE were supposed to take part in the combat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they were supposed to monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, they were monitoring, you could hear that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Another thing I wanted to ask you: You stated that you heard that during the attack 30 "terrorists" were killed. Who did you hear this from, this that was put under the quotation marks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we talked among themselves -- us, the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Further on you said -- further on you said you went to the village of Novaki -- all right, this is irrelevant here. Where is this village of Novaki?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the vicinity of the village of Trnje, and that is a Serbian village, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In which way did you come there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is a road from Prizren to Suva Reka, and at one point you have to turn left in the direction of some vineyards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the village of Novaki?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we stopped there for a short period, and then we went on. There was a school, some of the officers went in, they had some talks, and then they -- then we moved on. Possibly there is one thing to say: While we were in Trnje, I went with my main commander to the barracks on two or three occasions in order to pick up some items, he needed some things. I don't know why. So along the way we would come by this village of Novaki.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I do not want to confuse you, but after -- we are at the period of the 18th or 20th of March. We have not reached the time of war yet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, maybe there was some mistakes concerning these dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Because I can see that in your statement you follow the chronology. I would like to know, you said that on the 24th of March, 1999, while expecting the NATO bombing, all the units were evacuated from the barracks in order to prevent them from being hit. So was your unit also evacuated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where did you move to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just below the barracks, below the military infirmary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 24th of March during the night. There was an air-raid alert.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to clarify this for myself and for the counsel, could I kindly have document 65 ter 61548. That is on page 48. I may have made an error. So this is document listed under 65 ter 615, and it is on page 48. It is supposed to be a map of the town of Prizren. So this is an atlas of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can't really find my way around, but I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me help you. This red line I believe on top right is the road leading to Suva Reka. Top left I believe is the road leading from Djakovica to Prizren. Then the next segment goes towards Sredecka Zupa; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, towards Brezovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the left-hand side down there is the road leading to Zur. Can you see on this map the barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where were the barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you mark that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Slow down, slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So this point. Okay. Can you explain what it is that you've encircled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, these were the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put number 1 here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If this were -- if these were the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And this military infirmary that you mentioned where you were evacuated, could you show me where that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was just across the road. I've put number 2 here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I can't see that. Okay. So this is where it was, across the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, across the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you said you spent the night of the 24th there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is where we were. There is quite a lot of space there, and my unit was in that infirmary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now while we have this map on, can you tell me, When you came back on March the 30th, and in your statement you explained that this location, did you stay here at this place indicated with a number 2 or did you move somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On March the 30th?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I believe that was the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are probably wrong. This was on the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Right this is when you were evacuated, but ... I don't believe that I made a mistake. This is on page 7 of your statement. Let us go through that now so that we do not have to bring the map back up. So you saw PJP and you came back, and now I do not want to mention the name of the captain. So it was the 30th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the 30th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the place that you referred to on the page 7 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will mark it with number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So 1 is the barracks; 2nd is where you moved to on the 24th; and 3 is where you believe you stayed on the 30th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know Prizren very well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether this place number 3 was near Culjani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know where Culjani is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the mechanical equipment of the company was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shall I mark that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No. Just tell me whether this was above or below this place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was along the road leading to Djakovica, and this is where one part of my unit was, the technical company was situated there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You don't seem to understand me. I'm not asking about the technical company of your unit. I'm asking about the company called "Mehanizacija" from Prizren. Was that above or below with respect to this relocation point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Below, on the other side of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the names that we have here on the map, indicating the neighbourhoods, I don't know if you know at all where this was. You're not family with Culjan in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about the sports hall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about that either. I know how to move around the town and find my bearings according to some buildings and streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: However, from this point that you marked 1, the barracks; 2, the infirmary where you moved the 24th; and number 3, where you moved on the 30th when you returned from the mission, my question is -- we can say that this is a residential area in the centre of the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost in the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it possible for trucks to pass through these streets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they can.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Through all the streets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Through all the streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is Drmisa Slani [phoen] a street there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You don't know that street very well, but you told us that this was the neighbourhood where all the Albanians lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there were also Turks, Muslims, and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I know about all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you that, for example, the family Serpin, a Turkish family lived there; then the Topoljani family, the Muslims; then the Kastrati family, the Albanians; the Rudis family, who were Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But you say that only Albanians lived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the beginning of this neighbourhood those were military buildings with flats for offices. It is possible that next to those apartment buildings were the Muslims and the Turks, but further on all the residents were Albanians. Also there were some gypsies there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, the army captured the houses that they needed for their requirements; am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you yourself, while these houses were liberated, did you go there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, I went with the army. The whole army went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you when you were looking for a place to billet. I'm asking about securing a premises for the army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wasn't there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now go back --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But before that, Your Honours, can this exhibit be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That, Your Honours, will be assigned D00112.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, we have come now to this action that took place on the 25th of March, 1999. You said what happened during the night between the 24th and 25th. Tell us what happened later, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went, my unit, went to the Trnje village, in that general direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you please be more precise. Tell me what you did, which road you took, and how and where you went.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was driving a truck, and I travelled with the army. I was driving my soldiers through the village of Novaki and vineyards to Trnje?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you took the road to Suva Reka, then you turned, if I'm right, left to Novaki, and then this road let you to Trnje. How long was this column that you travelled with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It wasn't very long. My unit had some five or six trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So in this operation, you went to the side where Suva Reka was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you said that you were in which combat group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you're now putting me in the 1st Combat Group that has nothing to do with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We're going to show you the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me explain something to you. I was in a combat group in 1998, and we're talking about now 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But you took part in this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking you. You were not a driver in this operation. You were an infantryman, and I'm asking you as an infantryman to which formation you belonged. Do you know that or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how to explain this to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say you travelled via Novak. Did any other military unit travelled towards Suva Reka and then proceeded beyond that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure. But there was one unit in the village of Novaki, but I don't know nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm not interested in that. From Prizren did the second part of your unit went towards Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does not necessarily mean that it was from my unit, but it was from my barracks. So some elements from my barracks -- a unit from my barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, this barracks was of that unit and that the commander was the man that we mentioned before, but let's move on. At what time did you arrive in the village that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Early in the morning at around 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You took your positions there and then you say that some teams were set up. Can you tell us more detail about these teams, how many there were, how many members were in each team? No, no, this is going to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that the witness started to utter a name, so therefore I would kindly ask to -- this to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My commander ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems that it was not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't finish uttering the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we proceed, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My commander had his non-commissioned officers and he assigned them to create teams. One non-commissioned officer had a number of soldiers assigned to him, and that was called a team.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Who were you in the group with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted) With a man.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that section should be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's going to be. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I believe that our time is up for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We must adjourn now for the day to resume tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. The court officer will give you advice. But I think it is important now that we go into closed session for the witness to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 14th day of May, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
